division_folding_hazard.summary: literal/constant-foldable divisors fold to reciprocal multiply even with FastMath OFF; all varying scalars enter as runtime data arrays to force true fdiv
division_folding_hazard.bitwise_probes: literal-vs-data-divisor paths diverge on a substantial fraction of values: pi(f32) ~39656/262144 (~15.1%) and 30/64 at d=3.0 measured by the B7-30 reviewer; independently re-verified post-trials by the author with a corrected probe (pi 39373/262144 = 15.02%, d=3.0 87113/262144 = 33.23%, 32/64 on a 64-value sample; full divisor sweep in llvm_ir_division.txt)
division_folding_hazard.correction_history: an earlier revision recorded 0/262144 differences; that probe was tautological - its 'divide' side used a scalar constructor whose literal divisor folds to the same reciprocal multiply as the comparison side, so both paths were multiplies. IR inspection (fdiv present or absent) remains the conclusive structural detector.
division_folding_hazard.mitigation_status: load-bearing: the kernel's data-variable divisor construction is what makes the reflection term bitwise-exact; without it ~15% of pixel values would diverge from the Numba baseline

contraction_conclusion: fp_contract effectively OFF: no FMA/fmuladd instructions, no fast flags on any float op; accumulation order preserved exactly as the Numba baseline (fastmath=False).
denormal_note: default LLVM denormal handling; no flush-to-zero flags present in IR; NaN/Inf/-0.0 payloads bitwise-matched against the baseline (adversarial_replay.json).
